visual.general_description: Single coronal grayscale abdominal MRI with two colored arrows pointing to bilateral suprarenal foci.
visual.detailed_description: The grayscale coronal image shows a central vertical spinal column, bilateral kidneys in the lower upper-abdominal region, a broad homogeneous organ at viewer-left and bowel/pelvic structures inferiorly. A yellow arrow on viewer-right runs upward-right toward a rounded gray suprarenal focus; a pale pink/off-white arrow on viewer-left runs upward-left toward the opposite suprarenal region beside the spine and beneath the large organ margin. The rounded viewer-right focus is visually more conspicuous. The top marker reads S and the lower marker I. A horizontal footer ruler has fine tick marks and endpoints 0 cm and 27 cm. Black margins surround the image, with no panel letters, lesion calipers or printed lesion distances.

caption_claims.value: Caption describes bilaterally enlarged ellipsoid/rounded adrenal glands, left larger, maximum left 38 mm and right approximately 27 mm. These dimensions are author-reported and not pixel caliper measurements.

evidence.quote: Despite broad-spectrum antibiotics and fluid resuscitation, her condition was progressively deteriorating; therefore, steroids were initiated in view of high suspicion of adrenal insufficiency due to refractory hypotension and hyponatremia. She was closely monitored in the ICU but did not need a vasopressor. Contrast-enhanced CT of the abdomen followed by MRI (Figure 1) revealed bilateral adrenal enlargement with heterogeneous high attenuation consistent with acute bilateral AH.

clinical_significance.statement: Authors use CT followed by MRI to support acute bilateral adrenal haemorrhage in the ICU septic-shock case.

limitations: Color arrows designate the source-caption adrenal regions; patient identity and side are grounded in case/caption text, not appearance.
Footer ruler is image scale context; no lesion-specific calipers appear. Do not derive exact gland/lesion dimensions from pixels.
Single selected coronal slice does not establish the full examination, hormone function, histology or follow-up regression.

visual.general_description: Single coronal grayscale abdominal MRI with one yellow arrow pointing to a left suprarenal focus.
visual.detailed_description: The grayscale coronal image shows a central spinal column, kidneys on both sides, a broad homogeneous organ at viewer-left and heterogeneous bowel/tissue inferiorly. One thick yellow arrow on viewer-right runs upward-right toward a suprarenal rounded focus immediately superior to the viewer-right kidney and adjacent to the central vessels. Top S and lower I orientation markers are visible; a horizontal footer ruler has fine tick marks and endpoints 0 cm and 28 cm. The upper lateral regions are relatively dark. The image has black margins and no panel letters, lesion calipers or printed lesion dimensions.

evidence.quote: An MRI (Figure 2) was done in three days' time, which identified a lesion involving the left adrenal gland; it measured 32 x 31 mm and showed no significant interval change in comparison to the previous study. In the given clinical setting, the most likely possibility was haemorrhage in the left adrenal gland.

clinical_significance.statement: Authors interpret the left adrenal lesion as most likely haemorrhage in Case 2; MRI shows no significant change compared with prior CTPA.
